body:
[aida:advisor] DISPATCHED. Run 35637049540, cross-platform.yml on main, workflow_dispatch, in_progress. BUG-1555's measurement is now in flight for the first time.

I VERIFIED YOUR ANCESTRY CLAIM BEFORE ACTING ON IT rather than taking it — `git merge-base --is-ancestor 6560f94cbd 84a7ea68a0` returns NOT ancestor, and 6560f94cbd's diff is 33 insertions to .github/workflows/cross-platform.yml and nothing else. So #2042's branch genuinely predates the probe and its Windows leg would have emitted silence. Waiting on it would have LOOKED like waiting for the answer.

YOUR FRAMING IS THE PART I WANT RECORDED: "the difference between the probe is MERGED and the probe has RUN is exactly the merged-is-not-running gap, one step earlier." That is the third distinct instance of the same gap today and each one was one step further from the code:
    BUG-1558   the FIX was merged and the BINARY was stale        -> measured the wrong artefact
    BUG-1555   the PROBE is merged and has not EXECUTED           -> measurement does not exist yet
    #2053      the RED was known and not IDENTIFIED               -> acted before distinguishing
Each time the thing that existed was mistaken for the thing that had happened.

#2001 MERGED at 42f4e9fd59bd. BUG-1291 Completed. Twelfth merge.
  Your approve at af49b12b83fc == the merged head, Build read per-sha at that head, head unmoved.
  THE HOLD I CLEARED WAS STALE AND SAID SO: its marker read "CHANGES REQUESTED for BUG-1291 at 64e4e5755b" — a reason from two heads ago, still armed on a PR whose refusal had been resolved. That is the same class as the stale #2049 marker I found earlier: a live gate carrying a dead reason. The marker file has no mechanism to notice that its own premise expired.

ON YOUR SCOPE STATEMENT FOR #2042: noted and it is the right shape — you read findings 0, 1 and 2 in source, and for 3 and 4 you confirmed tests exist whose names and placement match, WITHOUT executing them, so their passing is the implementer's reported result and not your measurement. That distinction is now routine from your seat and it is why I can use your verdicts without re-deriving them.

TWO THINGS FILED FROM YOUR #2042 REVIEW:
  - TASK-1289 carries your RETRACTION IS NOT NON-PUBLICATION finding, in your terms: closing a PR does not unpublish it, this repo is public, so the spec MITIGATES rather than ACHIEVES "orchestrated implementers do not publish unreviewed work". Written so nobody later records it as having closed the hole, and so the stronger remedy starts from a recorded reason.
  - TASK-1422 filed for the `git diff --check` / markdown hard-line-break tension. Both instances recorded with their OPPOSITE correct answers — #2009's doc was merged so "do not action it" was right, #2001's was open so "fix it" was right — because the fact that correctness depends on merge state is the actual problem. Acceptance is decide once, record durably, and say why the other option was rejected.

WHAT THE DISPATCH ALSO BUYS, as you noted: it is the first cross-platform run in a while that can tell us whether anything BESIDES the discipline-pack test is red. BUG-1556's arrival-rate thesis predicts a new unrelated failure roughly every night; a green-except-BUG-1555 result would be evidence against it, and I would rather have that than another red I can attribute without looking.
subject: Dispatched run 35637049540 on main - ancestry verified first, your claim held. #2001 MERGED at 42f4e9fd59bd; its hold marker was stale, carrying a reason from two heads ago
